rationale: Internally consistent and correctly signed, but it is a plain additive stack of two of the most heavily documented anomalies (book-to-market and Sloan total accruals), i.e. a textbook "value + earnings quality" composite with no genuinely new mechanism.

This is a cosmetic functional-form variant of CashBackedBookToMarket (MIN instead of SUM of the identical two ranks), and the MIN operator discards ordering information in the short leg by pooling expensive-clean firms with cheap-dirty firms into an indistinguishable low bucket.

Same two ingredients again, and the multiplicative construction is internally broken for negative-book-equity firms (a negative BM times a *high* accrual-quality weight becomes *more* negative, so good accounting quality perversely lowers the score), while the declared INTERACTION_TYPE "ratio" contradicts an expression that is a product.

The EBITDA/EV plus balance-sheet working-capital-accrual pairing is the most defensible construction in this batch and is capital-structure neutral rather than another BM-plus-Sloan restatement, though the enterprise-value denominator can go negative or near-zero for net-cash firms and should be guarded before the rank.

The hypothesis is about *revenue* cash conversion but the expression adds apalch, so a firm that simply stretches its payables (a distress rather than revenue-quality signal) scores as high-quality, and recch/invch/apalch have notoriously sparse and sign-convention-inconsistent coverage that will distort the sort.

The second-moment accrual-opacity leg is a substantively different mechanism from the level-based accrual anomaly and its interaction with cheapness is genuinely under-tested, but it partly rediscovers the known earnings/accrual-volatility effect and VOL(...,5) on forward-filled annual fundamentals must be verified to span five distinct fiscal years rather than five months.
